About me

Energy modelling with a purpose

I'm a building energy efficiency engineer specialised in dynamic thermal simulation and green building certification.

At SustainWay in Casablanca, I build whole-building energy models in IES-VE, DesignBuilder (EnergyPlus) and TRNSYS, and run the energy studies behind LEED, EDGE and HQE certification projects.

For my master's thesis, I worked on the update of Morocco's building energy code (RTCM v1 → v2) for AMEE: 7 building types simulated across 20 cities, combined with national weather service data to propose a new climate-energy zoning of the country.

I like work where careful modelling turns into a real decision: a better envelope, a lighter system, a lower energy bill.

  • DegreeMaster, Green Buildings Engineering & Energy Efficiency, UM6P

Projects

Final-year project (PFE) · SustainWay for AMEE, with DGMMar – Jul 2026 · Casablanca

Updating Morocco's climate zoning for the RTCM

The RTCM, Morocco's thermal building code, sets how much energy new buildings may use for heating and cooling. It rests on a map of the country's climate zones, built from 1999–2008 weather data. Since then, summers have become hotter and heatwaves more frequent, so the map needs updating, roughly every ten years.

My role was to make the buildings speak:

  1. ModelBuilt 7 representative Moroccan building types in IES-VE from plans and sections, from housing to a hospital, with code-compliant envelopes, schedules and ASHRAE 62.1 ventilation.
  2. SimulateRan dynamic thermal simulations in 20 cities across the country with 2025 hourly weather, 140 annual runs in total.
  3. AnalyseCompared heating and cooling needs and comfort by zone, then checked that the new zoning reflects how buildings respond to today's climate.

Supervised by Pr. El Mehdi Laadissi (UM6P) and Mme Wiam Samir (SustainWay).

  • IES-VE
  • Dynamic thermal simulation
  • Parametric analysis
  • ASHRAE 62.1
  • RTCM

End-of-studies internship · Ciments du Maroc (HeidelbergCement Group)2023 · Laâyoune
About the company

Ciments du Maroc, part of the HeidelbergCement Group, is the second-largest cement producer in Morocco and a leader in ready-mix concrete and aggregates through its subsidiary Betomar. It runs three plants (Aït Baha, Safi and Marrakech) and grinding centres in Laâyoune (Indusaha) and Jorf Lasfar.

Raising the renewable share of a cement plant

The Indusaha cement grinding plant draws its electricity from two sources: its own wind farm, running since 2011, and the national grid (ONEE). The wind farm already covers about 67% of the plant's annual needs and saves around 2,000 t of CO₂ a year, but wind is intermittent. I analysed the plant's consumption data from both sources and proposed a hybrid wind and solar PV system with battery storage to cut the paid grid share.

Today · wind farm67%
Target · wind + PV + storage≥ 85%
  • Load analysis
  • Wind–PV hybrid
  • Battery storage

First internship · Energie Eolienne du Maroc (EEM)2022 · Laâyoune
About the company

Energie Eolienne du Maroc (EEM) develops, builds and operates wind farms in Morocco, including the Foum El Oued wind farm, and contributes to the country's energy transition.

Failure analysis of wind turbine power converters

My first field experience. I studied failures of the static power converters on the Siemens SWT-2.3 turbines of the Foum El Oued wind farm. These converters turn the turbine's output into electricity ready for the grid, so when they fail, production and revenue drop.

  1. StudyMapped how the converters work, from the turbine to the MV/HV substations.
  2. FMEAIdentified each failure mode and scored its occurrence, severity and criticality (AMDEC method).
  3. AdviseRecommended preventive maintenance actions to reduce failures and extend converter life.
  • FMEA / AMDEC
  • Siemens SWT-2.3-101
  • Power converters
  • Preventive maintenance
Module project · Energy Efficiency in Buildings · UM6P SAP+D2025 · Marrakech

Villa Targa: bioclimatic analysis and energy optimisation

Energy assessment of a villa under construction in Marrakech, a hot and dry climate where cooling needs dominate. The goal was to check the existing passive solutions and propose better ones suited to the local climate.

  1. AnalyseClimate study of Marrakech with local weather data, bioclimatic and psychrometric charts.
  2. SimulateBuilding model and energy simulation in Binayate, evaluating the existing passive solutions.
  3. OptimiseCompared several improvement scenarios to cut cooling needs and improve comfort and code compliance.

Solutions studied

  • XPS roof insulation
  • Rock wool wall insulation
  • Double glazing + solar shading
  • Thermal mass
  • Cross & assisted ventilation
  • Radiative roof cooling

Supervised by Pr. Brahim Benhamou.

Multidisciplinary project · Built Environment · UM6P SAP+D2026 · Marrakech

Energy and airflow simulation of a villa: TRNSYS & CONTAM

Coupled thermal and airflow modelling of a villa in Marrakech, to measure how construction choices, ventilation and air leakage affect energy needs and thermal comfort, then compare improvement scenarios.

  1. Model3D model of the villa and definition of the thermal zones.
  2. SimulateDynamic thermal simulation in TRNSYS and airflow simulation in CONTAM, coupled for a more realistic result.
  3. AssessThermal comfort measured in degree-hours (DH), based on the PMV / PPD indices.
  4. ImproveCompared envelope scenarios: insulation, glazing, airtightness and solar shading.

Supervised by Pr. Zaid Romani and Pr. Mohammed Ahachad.

Module project · Smart Building Management · UM6P SAP+D2025

Connected classroom: real-time supervision with Home Assistant

A complete smart supervision system for a university classroom, with live monitoring, home automation and automatic comfort and safety scenarios.

  1. Set upHome Assistant hosted on a virtual machine (VirtualBox), accessible on the local network.
  2. ConnectTemperature, humidity, light, gas and water-leak sensors, a smart plug, a smart bulb and a camera, linked through Smart Life and Tuya IoT.
  3. VisualiseAn interactive dashboard and a 3D model of the classroom (Sweet Home 3D) showing each sensor in place, in real time.
  4. AutomateScenarios for comfort and safety, listed opposite.

Supervised by Pr. El Mehdi Laadissi.

Bachelor's final project · EST Essaouira2024 · Smart building

Solar-powered smart building prototype

A small-scale building prototype combining thermal insulation, renewable energy and automatic control, to reduce energy use while keeping indoor conditions comfortable.

  1. CompareTested three insulation materials, wood, polystyrene and cardboard, and measured how much each one lowers the indoor temperature compared with outside.
  2. MeasureTwo temperature sensors, one outside and one inside, record both temperatures and show the gap between them.
  3. ControlAn Arduino program switches on an indoor fan when the inside temperature goes above a set limit.
  4. PowerThe whole system runs on a solar panel mounted on the roof, with a charge controller.
  • Arduino
  • Temperature sensors
  • Insulation materials
  • Solar PV
  • Automatic ventilation
